Reading List

This page contains the books that I either currently am, have, or want to read. I have a sneaking suspicion the "want to read" category is going to far outweight the rest for awhile. There's just so much I've been wanting to read lately!

This also isn't necessarily going to be an ordered list, nor is it going to contain everything I've ever read. As I get time, I'll try to go back and add books that I've previously read but for now, I'm just going to add books as I get to it.

I've also found a replacement for Goodreads that I've been using to track my books. It's called Hardcover and so far it's been really nice! Feel free to use my referral link and follow me on there!

Books I am currently reading

  • Executed - R.R. Haywood A thrilling time travel series, this time with a couple of new faces in the mix. Time travel can be tricky to tackle, but so far this one seems to be handling it just fine. It's been keeping me on the edge of my seat for quite a while now!
  • The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook - Matt Dinniman Fourth floor here we come! This was started out hot with the fight in the subway car and I only suspect things are going to heat up more as sponsorships start to come into play. Excited to see where this one goes!

Books I have finished

  • Red Rising - Pierce Brown I can't believe I slept on this one for so long, it had been sitting on my shelf for years waiting for me to pick it up. Once I did, I finished it in what felt like 4 days (which is nuts for me, I'm a slow reader generally). The story of Darrow is absolutely captivating and the author has done an amazing job building this world up.
  • Golden Son - Pierce Brown The second entry in the Red Rising series, this one ups the ante even more and propels the story to new heights even greater lows. The internal struggles that Darrow is undergoing are even more complex than in the first book. I just received the sequel to this in the mail, looking forward to getting it started!
  • The Color of Magic - Terry Pratchett Who let me live under this rock for so damn long?!? I'm a quarter of the way through this book (as of 2025-09-28) and I am loving everything about this story so far. Twoflower is the most oblivious person ever and watching Rincewind try to follow along and keep up so far has been wonderfully hilarious. I've already got the next two books sitting my shelf waiting for me to finish this one. I finished this on 2025-09-30 and it was so lovely!
  • Consider Phlebas - Iain M. Banks This one was an incredible ride. Everything I've read said that the general consensus is this is the weakest book in the Culture series. If that's the case, then I'm certainly in for a great experience because I loved this book! There were a couple slow moments, and I do think the ending on Schar's World lasted just a little too long, but overall I loved this from start to finish. While I do think the Schar's World section could have been pared down just a bit, it also helped to build the ambiance for the location nicely.
  • Morning Star - Pierce Brown I finished this one so quickly that I never had a chance to update this page in time. I could now put this book down. It was a great end to the proper trilogy for Red Rising. I'll get to Iron Gold eventually, but I'm going to let this one simmer for a bit before I come back to this universe.
  • The Shining - Stephen King This was an excellent read and a real nail biter all the way through. I loved how well-paced the tension was and you could really feel the descent into madness here. Just an excellent story. I've got the sequel on the shelf, but that's for another time.
  • Red Team Blues - Cory Doctorow This one was a fun, quick read. I love Cory's posts and this book, while a little on the unbelievable side at times, was still a fun one. Looking forward to picking this series up again.
  • Dungeon Crawler Carl - Matt Dinniman Well, I'm obsessed and it's only the first book. This was a thrill through and through. Here's hoping that the rest of the series keeps this going. I can certainly see why it's been consistently topping the charts on Hardcover though.
  • The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - Jack Bogle I've been taking a closer look at my overall investing portfolio and the ideas in this book really resonated with me. Over a long term horizon, investing low-cost index funds with a buy-and-hold mindset - no matter what happens - will almost asuredly lead to positive outcomes.
  • Carl's Doomsday Scenario - Matt Dinniman Yup, so far, this is shaping up to be one of my favorite series. Even if this book only covered a single floor, it kept the pace up incredibly well and threw in a bunch of new mechanics that are well thought out and add some fun spice to the series. As soon as I finished reading this, I bought the next book and started it though!
  • Extracted - R.R. Haywood A very interesting beginning to a time travel series. I got this one off of a recommendation from Kev Quirk. In short, a scientist created a time machine to fix something that occurred in his past, but in doing so he unleashed a future where the world ends. The main characters here are in a fight to figure out how they can stop this - but first, they have to come back from the dead and understand how this works to begin with. This is the first of three books, and definitely does a great job at setting the stage for an excellent story in the next book. There's a ton of character building in this one, and it's really well done in my opinion.

Books I want to read

  • The Children of Time - Adrian Tchaikovsky
  • Hyperion - Dan Simmons
  • The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet - Becky Chambers
